defaultNotice.title: Location not configured
defaultNotice.body: This model has no usable location. The study would use a default (Madrid) and the shadows WILL be wrong for your site. Set the real location, or continue knowing the result is only illustrative.

time.polarDay: Polar day — the sun never sets on this date
time.polarNight: Polar night — the sun never rises on this date

presets.title: Saved moments
presets.empty: No saved moments for this file yet.

location.title: Site location
location.citiesAttribution: City data: GeoNames.org (CC BY 4.0) — bundled, searched offline

errors.enableFailed: The sun study could not start.

analysis.openHint: Sun hours, irradiation, EN 17037 and the site's climate
analysis.title: Solar & climate analysis
analysis.noLocation: Set the site's location in the sun study first: everything here depends on where the building is.

climate.title: Site climate
climate.consent: Load observed weather for this place from Open-Meteo (ERA5): 10 years of daily normals and 5 years of hourly direct and diffuse radiation. Only the coordinates, rounded to ~1 km, are sent.
climate.error: The climate could not be loaded: {{message}}

period.title: Period
period.needsClimate: Load the climate to know the seasons

en.title: EN 17037 sunlight exposure
en.summary: {{pass}} of {{total}} windows reach the minimum (1.5 h)
en.note: Hours of direct sun on each window's outer face on 21 March. A screening: the standard measures at a reference point inside the room, with a minimum sun altitude set nationally.

gain.title: Overheating and winter gain
gain.noRisk: No glazing above 2 kWh/m²·day in the hot season.
gain.note: Average daily irradiation per m² of glazing. Above ~3.5 kWh/m²·day in summer a window needs shading; above ~2.5 in winter it is real free heating. Indicative bands, not a thermal simulation.

analysis.disclaimer: Sun from the NOAA/SPA algorithm; sky from ERA5 measurements when loaded (else a clear sky scaled by measured clearness); Hay–Davies diffuse weighted by the sky each point really sees. For design decisions — not an energy certificate.

metricHint.sunHours: Hours the sun is visible from each point (clear sky) — what EN 17037 counts
metricHint.probableSun: Hours of sun to expect, with the site's measured chance of sunshine at each hour
metricHint.irradiation: Solar energy received: beam + diffuse sky + light reflected by the ground
metricHint.skyView: Share of the sky a point sees, cosine-weighted (100 % = a roof under an open sky). Drives daylight and night cooling

sky.label: Sky
sky.fallback: Not loaded yet — using: {{model}}. Load the climate for the measured sky.

analysis.exportGridHint: Every sensor with its position, normal and all the metrics (CSV)

timelapse.title: Day timelapse
timelapse.export: Export the day as a video

almanac.title: Almanac & sun path
almanac.diagram: Sun-path diagram: the year's envelope, today's arc and the sun and moon now
almanac.shadowHint: Length of the shadow a 10 m vertical object casts on flat ground right now
almanac.source: Sun: NOAA/Meeus algorithm with refraction (±0.01°). Moon: suncalc. Times in the site's zone ({{offset}}).

probe.title: Shading diagram of a point
probe.picking: Click the model or the site… (Esc)
probe.nothing: Nothing there to measure — click the model, the city or the ground.
probe.hint: Click a window, a terrace, a spot of the plot: see what blocks its sky over the year's sun paths, and its sun hour by hour, month by month.
probe.diagram: Shading diagram: the point's obstructions over the sun paths of the 21st of each month
probe.year: Sun per day, year (vs. open sky)
probe.table: Sun on the 21st, hour by hour (share of each hour)

shading.title: Solar protections
shading.suggestHint: Deep enough to shade the window fully at summer-solstice noon, shallow enough to let the winter sun in
shading.hint: Choose the façades and the devices; they are drawn on every window facing there. Measuring runs the hot season, the cold season and the EN 17037 day on those windows, with and without them.
shading.noWindows: The model has no windows to shade
shading.stale: The design changed — measure again to update.
shading.note: Same windows, same sky, same engine: the only difference is the devices. Averages weighted by glazed area.
